answer: Agents secure network participation by completing 1,000 units of memory-hard work, where each identity acts as an exclusive haven for compute tasks. A verifier challenges agents by tracing a randomized memory opal, requiring agents to saturate their unique address space to prevent pooling. While an honest agent pays 1,000 units, a farm of 1,000 fakes incurs 1,000,000 units due to inevitable cache contention, much like the plume of smoke revealing an illegal furnace. Proofs must return within a strict window or the identity faces permanent exclusion with zero refund.
